title: Review: crypto2dev shim (post-fix pass)
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — one stale API doc comment creates a regression trap; one open-inside-mutex inconsistency creates latency risk under device unavailability. Code correctness is otherwise solid.
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug.
Uncertainty driven by: (1) All testing is against the software simulator — the real /dev/crypto2dev device may return different errno values or have different edge-case behavior for the INIT/FINALIZE/read protocol; (2) ECDSA key lifetime: ecc_key objects with devCtx fds are not tracked centrally; double-free is possible if a key is copied by value (wc_ecc_copy) and both copies are freed; (3) TLS 1.3 transcript-hash safety is tested via g_tls_safe_mode behavior (SHA-256 fallback KAT) but not via an actual TLS 1.3 handshake; the wc_Sha256Copy failure path exists in theory but has not been exercised.
Would raise confidence if: (a) integration test against real /dev/crypto2dev hardware with all KATs passing; (b) wc_ecc_copy behavior under WOLF_CRYPTO_CB_FREE confirmed (does it call FREE on both copies?); (c) actual TLS 1.3 handshake test with hardware HMAC and software transcript hash completing without error.
